Light Workbench

Current SQL Server insertion-loss testing workflow

Scope: This guide covers the normal hardware IL run using an ILM/OP815 and a supported Santec OSX-100 or OSX-150. The Red Light Test, standalone Live IL Reading, and Power Measurement Diagnostics are separate non-run tools.
Data storage: New accepted run data is stored in SQL Server. Existing CSV/JSON runs can still be opened for legacy review, but they are not writable database runs and are not silently uploaded.

1. Understand the main screen

Header

  • Select SM (1310/1550) or MM (850/1300).
  • Review the connected hardware identities.
  • Connect all hardware or one device at a time.
  • Check the advisory Database status.

Left column

  • Enter Hardware test setup information.
  • Choose the channel plan and run purpose.
  • Review the readings table and run/result status.

Right column

  • Shows current readings, controls, and Reference.
  • Shows analysis, replacements, and Run information.
  • The lower information area scrolls independently.

Hardware test setup can be collapsed, and the center splitter can be moved, to give the readings table more room without clearing entered values.

Database status: The top-row indicator checks in the background at startup and approximately once per minute. Green Database: Ready means the last check succeeded; Checking... means a check is running, and red Database: Unavailable means it failed. Hover for details or click to check again. The monitor does not hold a permanent connection, and Ready does not guarantee that a later save will succeed.

2. Select the wavelength mode and connect hardware

  1. Connect the equipment physically. Connect the ILM/OP815, the switch, USB cables, and the approved optical test arrangement. Close Santec Terminal or any other program holding the switch's VISA resource.
  2. Select SM or MM. Use the two radio buttons in the header. SM measures 1310/1550 nm; MM measures 850/1300 nm. The application trusts this operator selection and does not infer the mode from the ILM serial, firmware, or model.
  3. Connect the hardware. Click Connect Hardware... to connect everything needed for a normal run. Use its menu only when you intentionally need to connect or disconnect the measurement hardware or switch separately.
  4. Verify the status panel. Both required devices must show a connected/available state before Start Run can proceed. The panel shows model and serial information when the device supplies it.
  5. Use ILM Remote Mode when needed. The checkbox is checked when Light Workbench controls the ILM. Clear it to return control to the ILM front panel without disconnecting the USB/DLL session, then check it again before resuming automated measurements.
  6. Resolve connection problems first. Use the detailed popup and Help > Support Logs if a device reports Error. Tools that use only one instrument may still operate when the other instrument is unavailable.
Mode timing: Select the wavelength mode before calculating a reference. Changing mode selects that mode's session reference and is blocked during active hardware work.

3. Complete Hardware test setup

FieldCurrent behavior
Main board serialRequired for a normal run. A connected supported OSX can fill this from its identity and trigger a background part-number lookup when no run is loaded or active.
Switch serialRequired and entered separately. Automatic main-board detection does not overwrite it.
Part numberRequired. Type it, select it, or use Lookup Part Number. The three-digit channel field determines the read-only front-panel channel count used by full passes, analysis, and COC export.
Operating bandSelect O band or C band. It is stored with the run.
Tested byEnter the operator's initials.
StationEnter the positive station number. New database runs require it; Admin Mode does not bypass this requirement.
Run numberUse this with the main-board serial to load an existing run. When a new database run is created, SQL Server allocates the next run number for the unit; check the number displayed after creation.
Run purposeProduction is the default; Engineering, Training, and Calibration are also available. Purpose is fixed for active or loaded runs. Production-only reports filter by purpose, but purpose alone does not exclude compatible measurements from replacement analysis or COC creation.
Admin Mode: An authenticated administrator may explicitly continue past missing descriptive metadata. It cannot bypass disconnected hardware, an invalid channel plan, a missing/mismatched reference, or the required database station number.

Part-number lookup is read-only: OSX-100 units (SM or MM) are searched under U:\Product Log\Units-COCs-Param Files\OSX-100; OSX-150 units use the sibling OSX-150 folder. A loaded run uses its saved model, not a different connected device. With no known model, lookup checks both folders and requires one unambiguous match; an unavailable folder makes that search incomplete. Resolve duplicate/model-mismatch messages or enter the verified part number manually. The lookup-folder action opens the appropriate model folder, or their shared parent if the model is unknown. Lookup never creates, edits, renames, or deletes files on the drive.

4. Calculate and maintain the reference

Session behavior: A reference belongs to the connected measurement session and selected wavelength mode, not to whichever run is displayed. Loading a database run or legacy CSV does not replace it.
  1. Make the approved reference connection and allow it to settle.
  2. Confirm the intended SM or MM mode is selected and the measurement hardware is connected.
  3. Click Calculate Reference in the Reference panel. Wait for both wavelengths to complete.
  4. Confirm Reference status reports a calculated reference for the current mode and connected measurement hardware.
  5. Reconnect the switch path for the run. Do not recalculate a reference while a hardware run is active.
Reference safeguards: A calculated power below -40.0 dBm is treated as a dark/disconnected reference and is rejected. A confirmed measurement-hardware disconnect clears the session references and requires recalculation. Returning the connected ILM to local/front-panel mode does not clear the reference, but recalculate if the optical path or source behavior was changed locally. Automated measurement remains blocked until ILM Remote Mode is restored. Disconnecting only the optical switch does not clear references. Manual reference authorization is available only in Admin Mode through Apply Manual Reference.

5. Understand the quality limits

Normal operators do not edit limits. The application selects the saved model/mode profile; authorized administrators can change profiles through Edit > Admin Mode... and Edit > Admin Config.... New runs snapshot the active criteria so later profile changes do not rewrite historical results.

Switch modelToo-good warningOptimization warningFormal failure
OSX-100Below 0.2 dBNoneAbove 0.8 dB
OSX-150Below 0.5 dBAbove 2.25 dB through 2.5 dBAbove 2.5 dB

These are shipped defaults, not a substitute for the run's saved criteria. SM and MM profiles are stored independently. Too-good and optimization conditions require review but do not make a row red or automatically invalidate a reading. A formal failure makes the row red. A negative IL reading after four-decimal rounding indicates a reference or connection problem; it may remain visible temporarily for troubleshooting but cannot be written.

COC boundary: COC validation is stricter at the exact failure limit: each wavelength must be below the applicable COC limit after four-decimal rounding. A value exactly at that boundary can therefore block COC creation even when the table does not classify it as above the formal-failure limit. Read the COC validation summary.

Administrator timing profiles and averaged readings

After enabling Admin Mode, open Edit > Timing Profiles.... Select an existing profile, or use New or Duplicate, then adjust the following and click Save Changes to save and activate the selected profile:

SettingMeaning
OPM wavelength settlingWait after setting the meter wavelength, before confirming it.
Laser source settlingWait after enabling the source, before the power-sample schedule begins.
Live update pausePause between completed automatic live readings, not the total time to measure both wavelengths.
Samples per wavelengthSelect 1, 2, or 3 power samples. Multiple samples are averaged separately for each wavelength before calculating IL.
Sample offsetsAbsolute times after source settling, in increasing order. For example, 200, 250, and 350 ms target those three offsets, not three successive delays. Hardware-call duration can make actual sampling later.

The current driver uses the arithmetic mean of the sampled dBm values. It does not average channels, mix wavelengths, or average accepted attempts from different runs. A failed sample does not become an accepted partial reading. The Standard profile uses 100 ms meter settling, 500 ms source settling, a 250 ms live pause, and one sample at offset 0 ms.

Timing changes require controlled validation: Faster settings can affect accuracy or stability; a shorter pause alone does not remove source settling or instrument response time. The active profile applies to future acquisitions, including reference calculation and standalone tools. New runs save a profile snapshot; continuation and retesting use that run's saved snapshot, not newly edited settings. Older runs without a snapshot use Standard. Do not change timing to bypass hardware safety constraints.

6. Choose the channel plan

ControlUse
Full configured passNormal production plan. It tests logical channels 1 through the front-panel count derived from the part number. A larger temporary switch configuration does not expand this required pass.
Single channelTests one selected logical channel.
Specific channels/rangesTests a comma-separated plan such as 1, 3, 7-10. Repeated entries are tested once.
Extra channels onlyOSX-150 only. Starts a separate supplemental run above the part-number front-panel count without requiring a completed front-panel pass. Useful for measuring spares later; see section 8. It does not collect front-panel channels or make a standalone COC dataset.
Choose channel order manuallyOptional full-pass workflow for scattered hardware. Select each next channel manually. A repeated accepted channel creates another attempt while the newest accepted attempt becomes the current table value.

7. Start and perform the run

  1. Click Start Run. Preflight checks the channel plan, required setup fields, SQL Server readiness, both hardware connections, and the authorized reference before creating or moving anything.
  2. Confirm the prompt. The confirmation identifies the run purpose and warns that the switch will move.
  3. Move the cable. Follow the active channel/physical-port message in Current readings.
  4. Wait for both wavelengths. Live Write Mode is enabled by default. It continuously obtains complete two-wavelength readings using the run's timing profile, including any scheduled averaging, then waits the configured Live update pause. Wavelength/source settling, sample offsets, and instrument/DLL response time all contribute to the total cycle.
  5. Review the pending reading. The displayed pair is temporary. Continuous updates never save a reading automatically.
  6. Click Write IL. Click Write IL or use its displayed shortcut, normally +. The complete pair is committed atomically to SQL Server. The worker advances only after the matching saved-reading acknowledgement; wait for the next channel prompt before moving the cable.
  7. Repeat. Move the cable as directed, review the complete pair, and write it until the selected plan is finished.
Manual reading option: Before starting a run, clear Tools > Live Write Mode if you want separate Read IL and Write IL steps. Read IL measures and displays both wavelengths; only Write IL commits and advances.
Atomic readings: Light Workbench never treats one wavelength as a completed channel. If measurement or database persistence fails, no partial pair becomes an accepted measurement. Follow the popup; do not assume a value was saved merely because it appeared on screen. A pending save failure keeps the reading available for retry: resolve the reported problem and use Write IL again as instructed, rather than repeatedly clicking or moving to another channel.

8. Test extra physical ports on OSX-150

There are two entry paths. After a successful automatic full pass covers every required front-panel channel, choose Test Extra Ports or Finish Run. This offer applies to new and continued automatic full passes, not manual-order or selected-channel retests. Alternatively, select Extra channels only before Start Run to create an independent supplemental run, even if no front-panel pass has been completed. Do not try to continue a completed front-panel run as an extra-only run.

Channel counts: The part number defines the front-panel boundary N. The SCPI-configured count M describes registered logical channels, not the installed physical capacity. A larger configured count does not expand the required front-panel pass. Accepted extra-candidate measurements, not an assumed total, establish which extras can be used by analysis.

Extra routing methodOperator expectations
CLI tunnelingDefault for new OSX-150 settings. Extras are routed directly starting at N + 1, without requiring them in the module map. Physical capacity is unknown: accept only installed, correctly connected candidates, and explicitly stop when there are no more ports.
SCPI mapped channelsAn administrator selects this when extras have already been registered through the approved external module-map process. Tests the finite configured range N + 1 through M and finishes at its end. It does not use CLI or offer No More Physical Ports.

The administrator selects the method in Edit > Admin Config.... An existing explicit SCPI setting is retained. The method is saved with the run and cannot change during continuation; there is no automatic fallback between methods.

  1. Start intentionally. Choose Test Extra Ports after the normal pass, or start a new Extra channels only run. A stopped/incomplete extra-only run can be continued using its saved method and accepted coverage.
  2. For CLI, check IP readiness. If the switch returns 192.168.99.10, the program warns that its IP appears unset. Set the IP through the switch's approved front-panel process, then choose Recheck IP. A LAN-address query failure also requires rechecking. The switch and PC must have an appropriate reachable network connection; setting an IP alone does not prove reachability. Finish Run or Stop Extra Testing leaves the candidate unrecorded.
  3. Follow the candidate prompt. Routing starts above the front-panel boundary; continuation skips already accepted extras. CLI queries the switch's current IP before each direct route. Normal front-panel channels still use SCPI.
  4. Resolve routing problems. A failed route must be retried or stopped. If the separate Physical-port route unverified dialog offers Proceed Unverified, use it only after independently confirming the actual route. Sending a command or receiving a response does not prove that a port exists.
  5. Measure and accept. Move the cable as directed, review the complete valid pair, then use Write & Continue. Temporary readings are not saved automatically.
  6. Finish accurately. In CLI mode, choose No More Physical Ports only when the current candidate is not installed. Stop Extra Testing stops without claiming the physical endpoint. SCPI mode ends when its configured extra range is covered. Never accept a nonexistent candidate merely because it produces a plausible reading.
Extra-port boundaries: Failed, dark, stopped, retried, or unaccepted candidates are not saved as accepted extras. Previously committed readings remain saved. Accepted extras can support replacement analysis, but they do not count toward front-panel completion and are never written directly as COC channel rows. OSX-100 does not support this extra-only/replacement workflow.

9. Correct the channel or retest

Change Channel...

Use this during an active normal run when the requested channel is not the one you need next.

  1. Click Change Channel....
  2. Enter the logical channel and confirm.
  3. Move the cable to the newly requested channel.
  4. Review and write the reading normally.

In an ordered full pass, choose whether to continue from the selected channel or resume the interrupted channel afterward. Change Channel is unavailable during the extra-port phase.

Retest selected

Use this after readings have been written:

  1. Select one or more completed rows.
  2. Click Retest selected.
  3. Move the cable when prompted, then review and Write IL.

The latest accepted attempt becomes the displayed value. Earlier accepted attempts remain in append-only database history. Use View Reading History... in Run information to review them.

10. Read the table, status, and analysis

AreaWhat it tells you
Current readingsThe active channel and the current complete wavelength pair. It remains temporary until Write IL succeeds.
Results tableThe loaded run's newest accepted attempt for each channel. Passing rows say Pass; low readings say Too good, please verify. Formal failures are red; too-good and optimization warnings appear in the Status column and Analysis panel without yellow row highlighting.
RunCollection progress for this run's saved plan: Not started, In progress, Complete, Incomplete, Interrupted, or Unknown. A two-channel verification run can be Complete at 2/2 without covering the entire front panel.
ResultSeparately reports Pass, Pass · optimization available, Pass · review recommended, Fail · recovery available, Fail · no measured recovery, Composite pass available, Supplemental run, Review required, or Not evaluated. This may use compatible assignment history, not just the rows visible in the loaded run.
PurposeShows whether the loaded run is Production, Engineering, Training, or Calibration.
Show readingsFilters only the visible table. It does not interrupt acquisition, alter analysis, or delete data.
Compare withAdds read-only comparison columns from another compatible run for the same unit. Comparison never changes either run.
AnalysisLists formal failures, too-good channels, and optimization warnings using the saved criteria for the run.

Hover over the Run or Result status for missing channels, failing channels, available compatible runs, and other details.

Composite pass available (green): The latest effective measurements across compatible runs cover all required front-panel channels and satisfy COC measurement eligibility. COC creation is available; it is never automatic. Output/template/metadata problems can still prevent export. A newer accepted failing retest overrides an older pass in both status and COC preparation.
Recovery available (amber): Measured spare candidates can address the failing channels, but the unit is not yet a verified pass. Complete the external replacements, record them, and accept post-replacement retests. No measured recovery means current evidence offers no qualifying recovery; it does not prove that repair is physically impossible. Supplemental run describes a partial/extra dataset when it does not establish a passing composite.

11. Finish, stop, and review a run

  1. Allow the plan to finish or click Stop run. Successfully accepted readings remain in SQL Server. A stopped run is marked accordingly rather than presented as complete.
  2. Review the post-run optimization offer. A completed eligible full pass may ask whether you want optimization recommendations. Yes opens the existing replacement analysis; No simply dismisses it. This is not a COC prompt.
  3. Load a database run later. Enter the unit's Main board serial and Run number, then use Load Run. Database Reports provides broader read-only searches across assignments, runs, measurements/retests, and replacements.
  4. Review attempt history. Use View Reading History... to see the original accepted reading and every accepted retest for the loaded database run.
  5. Open legacy data when needed. Open Existing CSV and File > Open CSV Run... load older file-backed data for review and export. A legacy CSV is not converted into a writable database run.
  6. Clear the workspace between units when needed. File > Clear Workspace... unloads the displayed run and resets setup fields, readings, analysis, comparison, and table content. It does not delete saved SQL/CSV data, disconnect hardware, change wavelength mode, or invalidate the current session reference. Finish any active acquisition, reference calculation, or database write first.
  7. Copy values when needed. Copy Raw Data... copies accepted channel/wavelength values as tab-separated text. It ignores the current table filter and does not create or modify run data.

Test timing and session history

Test timing: Run information shows saved Active, Elapsed, and Stopped time, the number of testing sessions, and timing quality. View Test Sessions... lists each start and stop in UTC. Stop/continue creates separate intervals so stopped gaps do not count as active testing. Active time includes cable movement and waiting while a test is running; it is not source-on time or repair labor. Saved checkpoints update about every 30 seconds and after accepted readings. Older runs may show unavailable or partial timing; interrupted runs use checkpoint-based estimates. Stopped time is unavailable when full timing is not confirmed. Reports also expose numeric seconds and distinguish summed test effort from covered clock time across compatible assignment records selected by the report filters.

Timing save failures: If the final timing/status could not be saved, use Retry Timing Save in Run information. Its duration is frozen at the stop, so waiting to retry does not add testing time. Resolve this before clearing the workspace, starting another test, or closing normally. Accepted measurements remain saved. A recent open session from another application cannot be silently replaced; after an interruption, wait at least 90 seconds from its last saved checkpoint before continuing. Closing forcibly can leave only estimated timing through that checkpoint.

Hardware pairing and mistaken runs

A database run belongs to one main-board/switch assignment. If Start Run detects a different pairing, review Use switch with this main board? carefully. Confirm only after the required external module-map reset/installation process is complete. Confirmation closes affected assignments, marks their unfinished runs stopped, and creates a fresh assignment with an identity map. Previous measurements, replacements, spares, and analysis do not carry into the new pairing; historical records remain available.

For an accidental run whose readings must not contribute to later analysis or COC, an administrator can use Void Run from Analysis... on an inactive database run and provide a reason. Voiding retains the measurements and history but excludes that run from effective calculations. There is no unvoid action. Purpose is not a substitute for voiding, and an older pass cannot be chosen merely to hide a newer accepted failure.

12. Replacement analysis and records

Analyze Replacements uses the latest compatible accepted front-panel and extra-candidate readings across the current OSX-150 assignment, not only the loaded run. The minimum worthwhile improvement is controlled in Edit > Admin Config... for OSX-150 and each wavelength mode, and defaults to 0.2 dB. Recommendations are advisory; a candidate's measured performance is not a guarantee of the result after installation.

Database analysis snapshots and recommendations are saved with their source evidence. Analysis History... lets you review saved results after reopening the application. New accepted readings, replacements, spare changes, run exclusions, or criteria changes can make an earlier snapshot stale. Recalculate rather than treating stale recommendations as current. A failed analysis save is not a successfully published snapshot.

Routing confirmation: On approved firmware, CLOSe? reports the active logical channel. Light Workbench compares it with the requested logical channel before measuring. The physical port shown or saved for a normal/replacement reading comes from the recorded assignment map, not from CLOSe?.

  1. Review recommendations. Compare Current IL with Candidate IL at both wavelengths. Current IL is the effective front-panel measurement; Candidate IL is the accepted measurement of the proposed extra port. Check the category and measured improvement as well.
  2. Complete the external reroute. Follow the approved physical repair and module-map procedure. Analysis and Manage Port Replacements do not perform it for you.
  3. Open Manage Port Replacements... In Record Replacements, choose Use Selected Recommendation or Add Manual Replacement. Select the logical channel and proposed replacement port. Current port and assignment/run context are supplied from the saved assignment. Normal replacements require evidence from an accepted extra-candidate measurement.
  4. Document the cause. Choose a Reason: Dirty/scratched fiber; Issue with terminated boot; Splicing issue; Break in fiber; or Unknown cause of high loss. Confirm the Operator, which defaults from Tested by. Use Additional details for free-text explanation.
  5. Queue and review. Click Queue Replacement for Save for each logical channel. Only one pending replacement per logical channel is allowed. Review the queued rows, current mapping, and Designated Spares tab before saving. Recommended spare selections are proposals until saved.
  6. Save once. Save commits the queued replacements and spare changes atomically; opening or canceling the dialog records nothing. Validation or save failure retains the queue for correction/retry. The application reloads the effective map and audit history after success.
  7. Verify the installed result. Use Start Replacement Verification Run... to test the logical channels still awaiting retest. Follow the cable prompts and explicitly write each complete pair. An old pre-replacement reading or the candidate's original reading does not verify the new mapped channel.
  8. Analyze again. Recalculate after verification to use the latest assignment evidence. Continue if a further recovery or worthwhile optimization is recommended. A passing dataset with no qualifying improvement available can be ready for COC; an unverified replacement or remaining failure is not cleared merely because there are no spares left.

Correcting documentation: Select a row in Current effective assignment mapping and use Correct Selected Mapping... to document a correction, reversal, or later mapping change. This adds an audited record; it does not delete earlier records or physically undo a reroute. Confirm the documented route matches the approved external work and obtain required post-change measurements. The Audit History tab retains prior records.

Replacement boundary: Light Workbench records the operator's documentation. It does not command the switch to change its permanent mapping, does not use CLOSe? to verify a replacement, and does not infer that an analysis recommendation was completed.

13. Write a COC explicitly

  1. Click Write COC... or use File > Write COC.... Completing or stopping a run never starts COC creation automatically.
  2. In Prepare COC, select the Context run. The program automatically considers all compatible persisted runs; there is no two-run limit or manual supplemental-run picker. Run purpose does not by itself block COC eligibility.
  3. Review the derived front-panel count and validation summary. Required channels must be present, valid, non-negative, physically consistent, and below the COC failure boundary after four-decimal rounding.
  4. Check contributing runs, excluded-run reasons, and channel provenance in the summary. The newest eligible accepted whole pair wins, even when it fails. The program cannot substitute an older passing pair or mix one wavelength from each attempt. Changed ports must agree with recorded replacements and have compatible accepted post-replacement retests.
  5. Click Validate and Write COC. For a database run, choose the output folder. Light Workbench selects the model/mode/capacity template and creates a new timestamped workbook without changing the template. If validation or export fails, follow its details; do not treat a failed attempt as a completed COC.

Database aggregation stays within one unit/switch assignment and compatible model, wavelength, metadata, and criteria context. Voided and superseded runs do not contribute. A fresh hardware pairing cannot reuse an older assignment's passing readings. COC preparation is a report view, not a new combined run, and does not modify source measurements or switch routing.

Supported templates: OSX-100 supports SM and MM COCs. OSX-150 supports SM COCs. Capacity 1-45 uses the 45-channel template; 46 or more uses the 48-channel template as a base. For more than 48 front-panel channels, the exported workbook adds matching channel rows and spans pages as needed. Extra physical ports are excluded from direct COC rows.

14. Support and troubleshooting

SituationOperator action
Hardware will not connectRead the complete connection popup, verify power/USB/VISA ownership, close Santec Terminal, and reconnect. Do not interpret every VISA code as proof of a physical disconnect.
Reference rejectedCheck the reference cable, seating, selected mode, and received power. A dark reading below -40.0 dBm cannot authorize a run.
Negative IL displayedCheck the active reference and current optical connection. The value cannot be written as valid data.
Database unavailableThe run or reading is not treated as successfully stored. Keep the application open, follow the popup, and contact support before repeating work.
Extra-port IP warningFor CLI, set the switch IP through its approved front-panel process, then Recheck IP. If it still fails, verify network reachability or stop extra testing; do not accept the candidate as measured.
Replacement awaiting retestRecord the correct mapping, take and write both wavelengths in a post-replacement verification run, then recalculate analysis. Check that the run belongs to the same assignment and is not voided.
Saved analysis is staleUse Analyze Replacements again against current assignment evidence. History preserves the earlier snapshot; it does not make its recommendations current.
COC blocked or failedUse the validation or technical details in the dialog. The local support log correlates explicit COC attempts for engineering review.
Engineering support neededUse Help > Support Logs to open the local logs folder, inspect logging status, copy its path, or export a support bundle.

Quick operator checklist

1. Select SM (1310/1550) or MM (850/1300). 2. Connect ILM/OP815, switch, and test cable. 3. Click Connect Hardware... and verify both device identities. 4. Complete serials, part number, band, initials, station, and purpose. 5. Confirm the derived front-panel channel count. 6. Calculate Reference for the selected mode and connected ILM. 7. Choose Full configured pass, Single channel, Specific channels/ranges, or an independent OSX-150 Extra channels only run. 8. Click Start Run and approve switch movement. 9. Move the cable to the displayed channel/port. 10. Wait for a complete two-wavelength pair; nothing is saved yet. 11. Write IL (+); wait for the save acknowledgement and next-channel prompt. 12. Repeat until the plan is finished or intentionally stopped. 13. For a completed automatic full pass, finish or intentionally test extras. For CLI, resolve any unset-IP warning before routing extras. 14. Review Run, Result, Analysis, and Reading History. 15. If replacing ports: analyze, complete external work, record, verify, and analyze again. A candidate reading is not a verification reading. 16. Use Write COC... explicitly when eligible. Compatible history is combined automatically; the latest accepted whole pair wins, not the best pass.
Light Workbench IL Reading Guide · Updated 2026-11-10 against application 1.36.0 source. This guide describes implemented workflows, not hardware qualification or completed acceptance tests. If the installed build differs, report the discrepancy to engineering before relying on an uncertain procedure.
